queries.hook: The weight of work that does not sit right, a mind that will not settle, and the phone still in hand when the day is over.
queries.diagnose: When the mind is not given one quiet minute, it runs after results it cannot hold; stress grows from a mind that has never been allowed to rest.
queries.steady: Praise and blame, success and failure, come and go; what is yours is the effort, and that is enough to stand on.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.meaning: Arjuna speaks to Krishna. He says the mind is restless, turbulent and stubborn. It feels as hard to hold as the wind. Krishna agrees. He says practice and letting go can train the mind.
verse.for_you: You are in a place where the mind will not settle. The phone is in your hand and the work is still in your head. The texts call this a mind that will not settle, and they do not blame you for it.
verse.try_today: Notice when the mind will not settle, and let it go.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own waiting room, and the mind will not settle.
asks: How do I practice letting go when the mind will not settle?
How can I let go when the work is still in my head?

verse.speaker: Bhasa
verse.setting: Two childhood friends meet again in old age; one admits he never found peace.
verse.sanskrit: उह्यमानमनन्तेषु चेतः कार्यमहोर्मिषु । क्षणमेति न विश्रान्तिं चिन्ताताण्डविताशयम् ॥ इदं कृतं करोमीदं करिष्यामीदमित्यलम् । कलनाजालवलिता मूर्च्छिता मतिपक्षिणी ॥
verse.line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
verse.translation: Carried along on endless great waves of tasks, the mind never gets a moment's rest; its depths dance with worry. 'This I've done, this I'm doing, this I'll do': so the bird of the mind, tangled in a net of reckonings, faints.
verse.why: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

prasang.title: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
prasang.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.
prasang.story_hook: They had been inseparable as boys, and when they met again they were old men with nothing to show.
prasang.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

verse.meaning: Years ago, two childhood friends, Bhasa and Vilasa, lived together in a forest hermitage. After their fathers died, they went their separate ways and spent decades in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks the other if he is well. The other admits there is no wellness left. He says the mind is carried along on endless waves of tasks.
verse.for_you: The phone in your hand is another list in that endless net. You are not behind because you are lazy. You are behind because the mind has been trained to see every task as unfinished. The stress is not the work itself.
verse.try_today: When the phone is down, let the mind stay empty for one minute.
verse.scene_line: You are an old friend admitting there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.
asks: How do I stop the mind from making new lists the moment I rest?

verse.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
verse.setting: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira how a golden swan answered the Sadhyas' question about the best way to live.
verse.sanskrit: विमुच्यमानः पापेभ्यो धनेभ्य इव चन्द्रमाः । विरजाः कालमाकाङ्क्षन् धीरो धैर्येण सिध्यति ॥
verse.line: Like the moon slipping out of clouds, the steady one waits for the right time and succeeds.
verse.translation: Freed from wrongs like the moon from dark clouds, spotless and steady, waiting for the right time, the wise one succeeds through patience.
verse.why: Self-control, calm under insult and truth are the best way to live.
verse.misuse: Waiting for the right time is active patience, not giving up.

prasang.title: The golden swan and the Sadhyas
prasang.summary: On his bed of arrows, Bhishma answers Yudhishthira's question about truth, self-control and forgiveness with an old story: the creator, in the form of a golden swan, met the Sadhya gods and taught them that self-control, calm under insult, truth and good company are the best way to live.
prasang.story_hook: A golden swan landed among the gods, and they asked it the one question they could not answer: what is the best thing a person can do?
prasang.lesson: Self-control, calm under insult and truth are the best way to live.

verse.meaning: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira about a golden swan who once spoke to the Sadhyas about how to live. The swan says that the wise person is like the moon slipping out of clouds. They are free from wrongs and steady. They wait for the right time and succeed through patience. The point is that self-control and calm under insult are the best way to live.
verse.for_you: You are holding praise and blame in your mind while you work. The phone keeps you in lists of what is done and what must come. The swan says your effort is what belongs to you. Let the right moment find you. Your part is to stay steady.
verse.try_today: Notice when the phone rings and let it ring once before you answer.
verse.scene_line: You wait for the right time while the phone still rings in your hand.
asks: How do I know when to act and when to wait?

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verse.sanskrit: नैव प्रार्थयते लाभं नालाभेनानुशोचति । धीरस्य शीतलं चित्तममृतेनैव पूरितम् ॥
verse.line: Not begging for gain, not grieving loss: a steady mind stays cool and full.
verse.translation: He does not pray for gain, nor grieve over loss. The steady one's cool mind is filled as if with nectar.
verse.why: Calm isn't found by chasing it or changing places; it is how you hold ordinary life.

prasang.title: The calm of the wise
prasang.summary: In a hundred verses Ashtavakra paints the inner peace of the wise: calm while busy, unmoved by gain or loss, praise or blame, at ease whether in the city or the forest. The restless, by contrast, chase peace and never find it.
prasang.lesson: Calm isn't found by chasing it or changing places; it is how you hold ordinary life.

verse.meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to Janaka, the philosopher king. The king has asked how a person can find peace. Ashtavakra says it is not a matter of location or effort. The wise person does not pray for gain, nor do they grieve over loss. Their mind stays cool and full as if with nectar.
verse.for_you: The four hours on the phone have left you in a loop of wanting and fearing. The verse says your mind can be full without chasing the next win or dreading the next loss. Let your effort be enough. Your part is the work.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment when the mind asks for nothing.
verse.scene_line: You sit with the day's outcome, neither begging for gain nor grieving loss.
asks: How do I let go of the need for a good outcome?
Can my mind be full without a result?
What does my steady effort look like today?

verse.speaker: Rama
verse.setting: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion.
verse.sanskrit: विविक्त आसीन उपारतेन्द्रियो विनिर्जितात्मा विमलान्तराशयः । विभावयेदेकमनन्यसाधनो विज्ञानदृक्केवल आत्मसंस्थितः ॥
verse.line: Sit somewhere quiet, let the senses rest, and give your full attention to one thing.
verse.translation: Sitting in a quiet place, senses at rest, self-mastered, pure within, one should contemplate the One with undivided attention, resting in the Self.
verse.why: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

prasang.title: Sit quietly, keep faith
prasang.summary: Rama describes sitting in a quiet place with the senses at rest until the mind becomes like a still ocean, and tells Lakshmana that until he sees the divine everywhere, devotion keeps it alive in the heart.
prasang.lesson: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

verse.for_you: Bring the mind back each time it wanders, with practice and letting go; make the mind your friend through steady practice.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: परिभ्रमसि किं मुधा क्वचन चित्त विश्राम्यतां स्वयं भवति यद्यथा भवति तत्तथा नान्यथा । अतीतमननुस्मरन्नपि च भाव्यसंकल्पयन् नतर्कितसमागमाननुभवामि भोगानहम् ॥
verse.line: Why wander, mind? Rest. Not replaying the past, not scripting the future, I take what comes.
verse.translation: Why do you wander about in vain, mind? Rest somewhere. Whatever is to happen happens just as it will, and not otherwise. Not recalling the past, not planning the future, I enjoy the pleasures that come to me unlooked-for.
verse.why: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.
verse.misuse: Not an argument against planning; it is for the worry loop once you have done your part.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Advice to the mind
prasang.summary: The poet talks to his own mind: why exhaust yourself pleasing others, why replay the past and script the future, why roam everywhere but within. 'So what?' asks what all our gains amount to.
prasang.lesson: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks to his own mind in the Vairagya Shatakam. He asks why it wanders about in vain, seeking approval and replaying the past. He tells it to rest somewhere. Whatever is to happen happens just as it will. He says he will not recall the past or plan the future, but will enjoy the pleasures that come to him unlooked-for. The verse proposes that the calm you want is already inside, and you can stop rehearsing outcomes once you have done your part.
verse.for_you: You are on the phone for four hours and the mind is still running. This verse says rest somewhere. It does not ask you to stop working, but to stop the part that scripts the future and replays the past.
verse.try_today: Let the phone rest for one hour before sleep.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own quiet corner, and the mind is told to rest.
asks: How do I rest the mind without stopping the work?
Where do I rest when the day is not done?

story.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
story.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
story.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
story.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

anchor.speaker: Janaka
anchor.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after overhearing wandering sages, rethinks his life.
anchor.sanskrit: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥
anchor.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
anchor.translation: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
anchor.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
anchor.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.
